report.title: Myers-Briggs: A Working Reference
report.scope: MBTI theory, instrument family 1943-2018, psychometric evidence, critiques and replies, alternatives, ethics and employment law
notInScope: personnel selection science beyond one comparison

claims.claim: The four MBTI scales are internally consistent
claims.keyEvidence: Cronbach's alpha .91 to .92 on the US national representative sample of 3,009; .845 to .921 across 193 studies 1999-2024
claims.caveat: Forced-choice format can inflate internal consistency as an artifact

claims.claim: The scales measure constructs also found in mainstream personality research
claims.keyEvidence: Four MBTI indices map onto four of the five factors: extraversion, openness, agreeableness, conscientiousness. Neuroticism has no MBTI scale
claims.caveat: Erford et al. (2025) found most correlations below r = .20, which is normally read as discriminant rather than convergent evidence

claims.claim: The four-letter type is stable over time
claims.keyEvidence: About 50% receive a different classification on one or more scales on retest; 35% had a different four-letter type after four weeks; about 47% identical after five weeks
claims.caveat: Scale-level correlations are better, .81 to .86 over 6 to 15 weeks

claims.claim: Scores on each scale form two groups, as type theory predicts
claims.keyEvidence: Distributions are single-peaked and centre-heavy across multiple studies; the 1998 item response theory rescoring did not produce two-humped distributions
claims.caveat: IRT theta estimates can look two-humped while preference scores look flat; this is a scoring transform, not evidence of natural groups

claims.claim: The 16 types exist as real underlying categories
claims.keyEvidence: Taxometric analysis of several Jungian instruments including the MBTI found no support for underlying types (Arnau et al., 2003)
claims.caveat: Rests substantially on one study, cited through Stein and Swan (2019)

claims.claim: Type predicts job or leadership performance
claims.keyEvidence: Four MBTI scales explained about 1% of variance in five leadership practices, R-squared = 0.01, n = 464
claims.caveat: One study, non-representative sample of Colombian business students, self-reported leadership practices

claims.claim: Type is inborn and fixed by adulthood
claims.keyEvidence: No mechanism offered for inheriting one of 16 preference-defined categories; retest instability points the other way
claims.caveat: Heritability of continuous traits is well established, but that is a different claim

claims.claim: Type dynamics produces measurable interactions between scales
claims.keyEvidence: McCrae and Costa (1989) found no evidence for the interactions the dominant-function idea requires
claims.caveat: Absence of demonstration, not proof of absence

claims.claim: The instrument adds predictive value over a Big Five measure
claims.keyEvidence: No published incremental validity study located; Pittenger noted the same gap in 2005

claims.claim: The instrument is useful as a shared vocabulary for differences
claims.keyEvidence: Publisher satisfaction surveys report 82% to 96% positive; Pittenger concedes value as a non-threatening introduction to individual differences
claims.caveat: Satisfaction is not validity; no controlled trial shows it beats a cheaper framework

claims.keyEvidence: 26% to 32% information loss per scale under IRT analysis; dichotomising one variable cuts shared variance by about .64 of r-squared, both by about .40

claims.claim: Adopting a type as an identity changes behaviour
claims.keyEvidence: Impression management mediated about 46.9% and ego identity about 45.2% of the indirect path from MBTI labelling to social anxiety, n = 469 Chinese adults aged 18-35

rules: The J or P letter says which function faces outward: J means the judging function (T or F) is extraverted, P means the perceiving function (S or N) is extraverted
The E or I letter says whether the outward-facing function is dominant: for E types it is, for I types the dominant is the other function turned inward
The attitudes shown for tertiary and inferior follow the alternating convention; Myers did not settle the tertiary's attitude
